items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: he said you're going to work with Roy Eldridge. Elton: Roy had 2 weeks up in Milwaukee, and he asked me did I want it, and I said, 'Yeah.'

ctx.x: called 'Slappy's' on 29th and Indiana. And after I got off my job downtown on Sunday, I'd pull by there. You know, and we just jammed all morning, to at least 1 or 2 o'clock in the afternoon. And Stitt would be down there, and he says to me, 'Man, I got a job for you if you want it.' He had [Don Rail] Anderson drumming, a pianist named Willie Jones, who, Willie incidentally, was playing that locked-hand style, and still is, Big Willie Jones -- he said you're going to work with Roy Eldridge. Elton: Roy had 2 weeks…
So we bought uniform jackets at least, and we went to Milwaukee with Roy Elton.
What kind of things were you playing?
